annotations.title: How a kind of product's prices moved

description:
How a whole category's prices moved between two dates, in one call: the biggest regular-price rises and falls, promotions starting and ending, member price changes (Tesco Clubcard, SuperValu Real Rewards, Lidl Plus) and pack-size changes, kept apart, with a summary over every product compared (average and median shelf change, counts of rises and falls) overall and per store.

shelf_rise and shelf_fall are changes to the regular price; promotion_started and promotion_ended are changes in what was paid while the regular price stayed the same (a product at 18 euro on promotion and 23 euro after is a promotion ending, not a 27.8% price rise); loyalty_change is a member price moving; pack_change is the same product in a different pack size, confirmed over three days of records (a smaller pack at the same price is a hidden rise); was_price_change is an offer running at both dates while only its "was" price moved, kept out of the shelf figures because nobody paid it. Averages are geometric, so a half-price offer starting and ending cancel out; average_member_paid_change_pct uses member prices where they apply.

Each mover returned costs one credit; the summaries are free.

category.description: An aisle name to narrow by.

from_date.description: The earlier date, YYYY-MM-DD (prices are kept since May 2026).

group.description: A kind of product: beer, cider, wine, spirits, alcohol, or any product type such as breakfast cereal, butter, coffee, crisps, nappies. Narrower words work too ('vodka', 'red wine').

kinds.description: Which lists to return. Left out: all seven.

limit.description: Most products in each list (default 10, at most 50).

query.description: Product or brand words, with or without group, e.g. 'guinness'.

rank_by.description: Rank each list by the percentage change (pct, the default) or the change in euro (eur).

store.description: One shop to look in only that one: aldi, tesco, supervalu, dunnes or lidl. Leave it out for all five.

to_date.description: The later date, YYYY-MM-DD. Left out: today.
